metadata.title: A Fully Homomorphic Encryption Scheme
metadata.framework: Ideal lattices; bootstrappable encryption; squashed decryption; sparse subset sum; worst-case/average-case reductions over ideal lattices
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: Registry lists the title as "Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices" (the STOC 2009 paper). The PDF at this BID is the corresponding Stanford Ph.D. dissertation, "A Fully Homomorphic Encryption Scheme" (Gentry 2009), which is the long version covering the same construction in more detail. Same author, same year, same construction.

nodes.name: Correctness of Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: $E$ is correct for circuits in $C_E$ if for any $(sk,pk) \leftarrow \mathrm{KeyGen}_E(\lambda)$, any $C \in C_E$, plaintexts $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_t$, and ciphertexts $\psi_i \leftarrow \mathrm{Encrypt}_E(pk,\pi_i)$: $\mathrm{Decrypt}_E(sk,\mathrm{Evaluate}_E(pk,C,\Psi)) = C(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_t)$ except with negligible probability.

nodes.name: Compact Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: $E$ is compact if there is a polynomial $f$ such that for every security parameter $\lambda$, the decryption algorithm can be expressed as a circuit $D_E$ of size at most $f(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Compactly Evaluates
nodes.statement: $E$ compactly evaluates circuits in $C_E$ if $E$ is compact and correct for $C_E$.

nodes.name: Fully Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: $E$ is fully homomorphic if it compactly evaluates all (boolean) circuits.

nodes.name: Leveled Fully Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: A family $\{E^{(d)} : d \in \mathbb{Z}^+\}$ is leveled fully homomorphic if all schemes share the same decryption circuit, $E^{(d)}$ compactly evaluates circuits of depth $\le d$, and complexity is $\mathrm{poly}(\lambda,d,|C|)$.

nodes.name: Statistical Circuit Privacy
nodes.statement: $E$ is circuit-private for $C_E$ if for any $(sk,pk)$, $C \in C_E$, and ciphertexts $\Psi$ encrypting $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_t$, the distributions $\mathrm{Encrypt}_E(pk,C(\vec\pi))$ and $\mathrm{Evaluate}_E(pk,C,\Psi)$ are statistically indistinguishable.

nodes.name: Semantic Security (CPA/CCA1/CCA2)
nodes.statement: $E$ is semantically secure against (CPA, CCA1, CCA2) attacks if no polynomial-time adversary $A$ achieves non-negligible advantage $|\Pr[b=b']-1/2|$ in the corresponding game.

nodes.name: Ideal Membership Problem (IMP)
nodes.statement: Given ring $R$, ideal $I$ and sampler $\mathrm{Samp}_I$ for $I$: challenger picks $b \leftarrow \{0,1\}$; if $b=0$ sets $x \leftarrow \mathrm{Samp}_I(R)$, else $x \leftarrow R$ uniformly. Guess $b$ from $(x,R,\mathrm{Samp}_I)$.

nodes.name: Augmented Decryption Circuit
nodes.statement: For $E$'s decryption circuit $D_E$ taking sk and ciphertext in $P^{\ell(\lambda)}$, and gate set $\Gamma$ over $P$, a $g$-augmented decryption circuit (for $g \in \Gamma$) joins multiple copies of $D_E$ via a single $g$ gate. Denote the set $D_E(\Gamma)$.

nodes.name: Bootstrappable Encryption Scheme
nodes.statement: $E$ is bootstrappable with respect to $\Gamma$ if $D_E(\Gamma) \subseteq C_E$, i.e., $E$ can compactly evaluate its own decryption circuit augmented by any gate $g \in \Gamma$.

nodes.name: Ideal Coset Problem (ICP)
nodes.statement: Fix $R$, $B_I$, $\mathrm{IdealGen}$, sampler $\mathrm{Samp}_1$ of $R$. Challenger picks $b \leftarrow \{0,1\}$ and $(B^{sk}_J,B^{pk}_J) \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R,B_I)$. If $b=0$: $r \leftarrow \mathrm{Samp}_1(R)$, $t \leftarrow r \bmod B^{pk}_J$. If $b=1$: $t$ uniform in $R \bmod B^{pk}_J$. Guess $b$ given $(t,B^{pk}_J)$.

nodes.name: Generalized Circuit
nodes.statement: For a $\bmod\text{-}B_I$ circuit $C$, the generalized circuit $g(C)$ is formed by replacing $\mathrm{Add}_{B_I}$ and $\mathrm{Mult}_{B_I}$ operations with ring-$R$ addition and multiplication.

nodes.name: X_Enc and X_Dec
nodes.statement: $X_{\mathrm{Enc}}$ is the image of $\mathrm{Samp}$ (so all ciphertexts lie in $X_{\mathrm{Enc}}+J$). $X_{\mathrm{Dec}} = R \bmod B^{sk}_J$ is the set of distinguished representatives of cosets of $J$ wrt $B^{sk}_J$.

nodes.name: Permitted Circuits
nodes.statement: $C_{E^0} = \{C : \forall (x_1,\ldots,x_t) \in X_{\mathrm{Enc}}^t,\ g(C)(x_1,\ldots,x_t) \in X_{\mathrm{Dec}}\}$. $C_E$ is a set of permitted circuits if $C_E \subseteq C_{E^0}$.

nodes.name: Valid Ciphertext
nodes.statement: $\psi$ is valid wrt public key $pk$ and permitted circuits $C_E$ if $\psi = \mathrm{Evaluate}(pk,C,\Psi)$ for some $C \in C_E$ and ciphertexts $\Psi$ each in the image of $\mathrm{Encrypt}$.

nodes.name: SVP, CVP, SIVP, BDDP
nodes.statement: For lattice $L$ of dimension $n$: $\gamma$-SVP asks for $v \in L\setminus 0$ with $\|v\| \le \gamma\cdot\lambda_1(L)$; $\gamma$-CVP given $t$ asks for $v \in L$ with $\|t-v\| \le \gamma\cdot\mathrm{dist}(L,t)$; $\gamma$-SIVP asks for independent $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ with $\|v_i\| \le \gamma\cdot\lambda_n(L)$; $\gamma$-BDDP is $\gamma$-CVP under the promise $(\gamma+1)\cdot\mathrm{dist}(L,t) < \lambda_1(L)$.

nodes.name: r_Enc and r_Dec
nodes.statement: $r_{\mathrm{Enc}}$ is the smallest value with $X_{\mathrm{Enc}} \subseteq B(r_{\mathrm{Enc}})$, where $B(r)$ is the ball of radius $r$. $r_{\mathrm{Dec}}$ is the largest value with $X_{\mathrm{Dec}} \supseteq B(r_{\mathrm{Dec}})$.

nodes.name: Decision BDDP for Ideal Lattices
nodes.statement: Fix $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(f(x))$, $\mathrm{IdealGen}$, sampler $\mathrm{Samp}_1$ of $\mathbb{Z}^n$. Challenger picks $b$, $(B^{sk}_J,B^{pk}_J) \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R,B_I)$; if $b=0$: $r \leftarrow \mathrm{Samp}_1(R)$, $t \leftarrow r \bmod B^{pk}_J$; else $t$ uniform. Guess $b$ given $(t,B^{pk}_J)$.

nodes.name: SplitKey Distinguishing Problem (Abstract)
nodes.statement: Challenger sets $(sk^*,pk^*) \leftarrow \mathrm{KeyGen}_{E^*}$ and $b \leftarrow \{0,1\}$. If $b=0$: $(sk,\tau) \leftarrow \mathrm{SplitKey}(sk^*,pk^*)$; else $(sk,\tau) \leftarrow \mathrm{SplitKey}(\bot,pk^*)$. Guess $b$ given $(\tau, sk^*, pk^*)$.

nodes.name: SplitKey Distinguishing Problem (Concrete)
nodes.statement: $(sk^*,pk^*) \leftarrow \mathrm{KeyGen}_{E^*}$ with $sk^*$ containing $v^{sk^*}_J \in J^{-1}$. If $b=1$, set $v^{sk^*}_J \leftarrow 0$. $\tau$ is $\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)$ vectors in $J^{-1} \bmod B_I$ with hidden subset $S$ of size $\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)$ such that $\sum_{i\in S} t_i \in v^{sk^*}_J + I$. Guess $b$ from $(\tau, sk^*, pk^*)$.

nodes.name: Sparse Vector Subset Sum Problem (SVSSP)
nodes.statement: Let $B_{IJ}$ be the Hermite normal form of $IJ$. If $b=0$: $\tau = \{u_1,\ldots,u_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)}\}$ uniform in $\mathbb{Z}^n \cap P(B_{IJ})$ subject to $\exists S$ of size $\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)$ with $\sum_{i\in S} u_i \in IJ$; else without constraint. Guess $b$ from $(\tau, sk^*, pk^*)$.

nodes.name: Sparse Subset Sum Problem (SSSP)
nodes.statement: For prime $q$: if $b=0$, $\tau = \{a_1,\ldots,a_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)}\} \subset [-q/2,q/2]$ uniform subject to $\exists S$ of size $\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)$ with $\sum_{i\in S} a_i = 0 \bmod q$; else without constraint. Guess $b$ from $\tau$.

nodes.name: Search SSSP
nodes.statement: Given $\tau = (a_1,\ldots,a_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)}) \subset [-q/2,q/2]$ uniform subject to existence of subset $S$ of size $\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)$ with $\sum_{i\in S} a_i = 0 \bmod q$: output $S$.

nodes.name: Inner Ideal Membership Problem (IIMP)
nodes.statement: Fix $R$, $B_I$, $\mathrm{IdealGen}$, real $s_{\mathrm{IIMP}} > 0$. $(B^{sk}_J,B^{pk}_J) \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R,B_I)$; if $b=0$: $x \leftarrow D_{I,s_{\mathrm{IIMP}},0}$, else $x \leftarrow D_{R,s_{\mathrm{IIMP}},0}$; $t \leftarrow x \bmod B^{pk}_J$. Guess $b$ given $(B^{pk}_J, t)$.

nodes.name: Modified IIMP (MIIMP)
nodes.statement: $(B^{sk}_J,B^{pk}_J) \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R,B_I)$; if $b=0$: $x$ chosen with $x \in I$ and $\|x\| < s_{\mathrm{MIIMP}}$; else same but $x \notin I$; $t \leftarrow x \bmod B^{pk}_J$. Guess $b$ from $(B^{pk}_J,t)$.

nodes.name: I-Hybrid Bounded Distance Decoding (HBDDP)
nodes.statement: Fix $R$, $B_I$, $\mathrm{IdealGen}$, $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}} > 0$. $(B^{sk}_J,B^{pk}_J) \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R,B_I)$, then $x$ with $\|x\| < s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$ and $t \leftarrow x \bmod B^{pk}_J$. Given $(B^{pk}_J,t)$, output $x$.

nodes.name: Ideal Independent Vector Improvement Problem (IVIP)
nodes.statement: Fix $R$, $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}} \ge 1$. Let $B_J$ be a basis of an ideal lattice $J$. Given $B_J$, output an independent set $B_{J^{-1}}$ of $J^{-1}$ with $\|B_{J^{-1}}\| \le 1/s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$.

nodes.name: Hybrid BDDP (HBDDP) over Ideal Lattices
nodes.statement: Fix $R$ and $\mathrm{IdealGen}$. $B^{pk}_J \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R)$, then choose $x$ with $\|x\| < s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$ and $t \leftarrow x \bmod B^{pk}_J$. Given $(B^{pk}_J,t)$, output $x$.

nodes.name: Worst-Case BDDP (WBDDP)
nodes.statement: Given $(B_M, t)$ where $B_M$ is a basis for an ideal lattice $M$ and $\mathrm{dist}(M,t) \le s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}}$: output $y \in t + M$ with $\|y\| \le s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}}$.

nodes.name: Ideal SIVP and Inverse Ideal SIVP
nodes.statement: Ideal SIVP: given basis $B_M$ of ideal $M$, output independent set of $M$ with norm $\le d_{\mathrm{SIVP}}\cdot\lambda_n(M)$. Inverse Ideal SIVP (ISIVP): output independent set $B_{M^{-1}}$ of $M^{-1}$ with norm $\le d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}}\cdot\lambda_n(M^{-1})$.

nodes.name: Leftover Hash Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a family of 2-universal hash functions from $X$ to $Y$. If $h \leftarrow H$ and $x \leftarrow X$ are uniform and independent, then $(h, h(x))$ is $\tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{|Y|/|X|}$-uniform over $H \times Y$.

nodes.name: Circulant Ring Expansion
nodes.statement: Suppose $x,y \in R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(x^n-1)$ and $z \leftarrow x \times y$. Then $\|z\| \le \sqrt{n}\cdot\|x\|\cdot\|y\|$.

nodes.name: Geometric Characterization of r_Dec
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a lattice basis and $B^* = (B^{-1})^T$. Let $r$ be the radius of the largest sphere centered at $0$ inscribed in $P(B)$. Then $r = 1/(2\cdot\|B^*\|)$. In particular, $r_{\mathrm{Dec}} = 1/(2\cdot\|((B^{sk}_J)^{-1})^T\|)$.

nodes.name: Rotation Basis from Nearly-Parallel Vector
nodes.statement: Let $t \ge 4n\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot s$ and suppose $v \in t\cdot e_1 + B(s)$. Let $B$ be the rotation basis of $v$. Then $P(B)$ inscribes a ball of radius at least $t/4$.

nodes.name: Dual-Inverse Length Relationship
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a rotation basis and $B^*$ its inverse transpose. Then $\|B^*\|\cdot n \ge \|B^{-1}\|$ (and conversely a comparable bound).

nodes.name: Generating an Inverse-Ideal Vector from a Dual Vector
nodes.statement: Let $w \in J^*$ where $J^*$ is the dual of ideal lattice $J$. Then one can compute $v \in J^{-1}$ whose rotation basis $B_v$ satisfies $\|B_v\| \le \sqrt{n}\cdot\|f\|\cdot\|w\|$.

nodes.name: Transference Lemma I (lambda_n via dual)
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be a (possibly fractional) ideal of $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(f(x))$. Then $\lambda_n(J^{-1}) \le \sqrt{n}\cdot\|f\|\cdot\lambda_1(J^*)$ (and related transference inequalities).

nodes.name: Transference Lemma II (lambda_n via determinant)
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be an ideal of $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(f(x))$. Then $\lambda_n(J) < n\cdot\|f\|\cdot\det(J)^{1/n}$.

nodes.name: Transference Lemma III (product ideal)
nodes.statement: Let $J,K$ be (possibly fractional) ideals of $R$. Then $\lambda_n(JK) < n\cdot\|f\|\cdot\det(JK)^{1/n}$ (with appropriate conditions handling singular factors).

nodes.name: Tweak 1: Short Inverse-Ideal Vector
nodes.statement: From an initial secret basis $B^{sk}_J$ that decrypts correctly for parameter $r_{\mathrm{Dec}}$, one can compute in poly-time $v^{sk}_J \in J^{-1}$ such that the rotation basis of $1/v^{sk}_J$ inscribes a ball of radius $\ge r_{\mathrm{Dec}}/(n^{2.5}\|f\|\|B_I\|)$, and decryption can be rewritten as $\pi = \psi - \lfloor v^{sk}_J\times\psi\rceil \bmod B_I$.

nodes.name: Tweak 2: Coefficients Within 1/4 of Integers
nodes.statement: If $\psi$ is a valid ciphertext after Tweak 2 (i.e., $\psi \in B(r_{\mathrm{Dec}}/2)+J$), then each coefficient of $(B^{sk2}_J)^{-1}\cdot\psi$ is within $1/4$ of an integer.

nodes.name: Rounded-Sum via Symmetric Polynomials
nodes.statement: Let $a_i = (\ldots,a_{i,1},a_{i,0},a_{i,-1},\ldots)$ be reals in binary mod $B_I$ with $\sum_i a_i \bmod 1 \in [-1/4,1/4]$. There is a $\bmod\text{-}B_I$ circuit producing $t+1$ integers with sum $\lfloor\sum a_i\rceil$ such that $r_{\mathrm{out}} \le (\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_{\mathrm{in}})^{t\cdot\mathrm{polylog}(t)}$.

nodes.name: Constant-Depth Sum of n Vectors
nodes.statement: Using a constant-depth circuit with polynomial-fan-in $\mathrm{Add}_{B_I}$ gates and constant-fan-in $\mathrm{Mult}_{B_I}$ gates, one can compute $\sum x_i$ for $n$ vectors when only one is nonzero, by XOR-ing them together (no carries).

nodes.name: Smoothing-Parameter Bound (cited)
nodes.statement: For any $n$-dimensional lattice $L$ and positive real $\epsilon$, the smoothing parameter satisfies $\eta_\epsilon(L) \le \sqrt{\ln(2n(1+1/\epsilon))/\pi}\cdot\|\tilde B\|$ for any basis $B$ of $L$.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussian Sampling Generates Most Probability
nodes.statement: For any full-rank $n$-dimensional lattice $L$ and parameters above smoothing, $\Pr_{x \leftarrow D_{L,s,c}}[\|x-c\| > s\sqrt{n}] \le ((1+\epsilon)/(1-\epsilon))\cdot 2^{-n}$.

nodes.name: Probability-Mass Ratio for Sub-Lattice
nodes.statement: Let $L,M$ be full-rank $n$-dimensional lattices with $M \subseteq L$. Then for $s$ exceeding smoothing parameters, $\rho_{s,c}(M)/\rho_{s,c}(L) \approx \det(L)/\det(M) = 1/[L:M]$.

nodes.name: Kummer-Dedekind Theorem
nodes.statement: For factorization $f(x) = \prod g_i(x)^{e_i} \bmod p$ in $\mathbb{F}_p[x]$, the prime ideals of $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ above $p$ correspond to the $g_i$, with norm $p^{\deg g_i}$ (under standard conditions).

nodes.name: Density of Prime Ideals (GRH)
nodes.statement: Assume GRH. Let $K$ be an algebraic number field. The number of prime ideals of norm in $[N,2N]$ is $\Theta(N/\log N)$ as $N \to \infty$.

nodes.name: v Lies in Translated Ball (RandomizeIdeal)
nodes.statement: The vector $v$ drawn in Step 1 of $\mathrm{RandomizeIdeal}$ lies in $t\cdot e_1 + B(s\sqrt{n})$ with overwhelming probability.

nodes.name: Bound on lambda_1(J)/r_Dec
nodes.statement: Let $B^{sk}_J, B^{pk}_J, v, B_K$ be generated by IdealGen as in Chapter 18.1. Then $\lambda_1(J)/r_{\mathrm{Dec}} = \mathrm{poly}(n)$ when $\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)$ is polynomial in $n$.

nodes.name: Lambda_1 Lower Bound for v Near e_1
nodes.statement: Let $v = e_1 + u$. Then $\lambda_1((v)) \ge 1 - \gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot\|u\|$.

nodes.name: Series Bound for 1/v
nodes.statement: If $\|u\| < 1/\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)$, then a geometric-series-type identity bounds the inverse of $v = e_1+u$ in $\mathbb{Q}[x]/(f(x))$.

nodes.name: Determinant of (v)
nodes.statement: Let $v = e_1 + u$. Then $\det((v)) \le e^{n\cdot\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot\|u\|}$. In particular, if $\|u\| \le 1/(n\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R))$, $\det((v)) = O(1)$.

nodes.name: Bootstrapping Yields Leveled FHE (Informal Theorem 1.3.1)
nodes.statement: If $E$ is bootstrappable, then for any integer $d$ one can construct $E^{(d)}$ that compactly evaluates any NAND-circuit of depth $d$, with public key size $O(d)$ times $E$'s and $\mathrm{Evaluate}_{E^{(d)}}$ polynomial in $\lambda$ and linear in circuit size; CPA-security is preserved.

nodes.name: Circuit Depth Bound (Informal Theorem 1.4.1)
nodes.statement: Suppose $X \subseteq B(r_X)$, $Y \supseteq B(r_Y)$, $r_X \ge 1$. Then $C(x_1,\ldots,x_t) \in Y$ for all $x_i \in X$ and arithmetic circuits with $\mathrm{Mult}$ fan-in $2$, $\mathrm{Add}$ fan-in $\le \gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)$, depth $\le \log\log r_Y - \log\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_X)$.
conclusions: $C(\vec x) \in Y$ for all $C$ with depth $\le \log\log r_Y - \log\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_X)$

nodes.name: Security of Squashed Scheme (Informal Theorem 1.5.1)
nodes.statement: If $A$ breaks the squashed scheme with non-negligible probability, then either $B_1$ breaks the original scheme or $B_2$ solves the SplitKey distinguishing problem with non-negligible advantage.

nodes.name: Decryption Circuit Depth After Squashing (Informal Theorem 1.5.2)
nodes.statement: After tweaks and squashing, the decryption circuit of $E$ has depth $c\cdot(\log|T|)^{1+o(1)}$. The scheme is bootstrappable when this is less than $\log\log(r_{\mathrm{Dec}}/2) - \log\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_{\mathrm{Enc}})$.

nodes.name: Security Reduction to BDDP/SIVP (Informal Theorem 1.6.1)
nodes.statement: If an algorithm breaks the somewhat homomorphic scheme with probability $\epsilon$, then there is a classical algorithm solving average-case BDDP over ideal lattices with approximation factor $(r_{\mathrm{Dec}}/r_{\mathrm{Enc}})\cdot\mathrm{poly}(n,\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R),1/\epsilon)$, and a quantum algorithm solving worst-case SIVP over ideal lattices with the same approximation factor.

nodes.name: Semantic Security of Abstract Scheme via IMP (Theorem 3.0.5)
nodes.statement: If $A$ breaks the semantic security of the abstract scheme with advantage $\epsilon$, then $B$ solves IMP with advantage $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Correctness of Leveled FHE Construction (Theorem 4.2.1)
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be bootstrappable wrt gate set $\Gamma$. Then $E^{(d)}$ compactly evaluates all circuits of depth $d$ with gates in $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ is universal, $\{E^{(d)}\}$ is leveled fully homomorphic.
conclusions: $E^{(d)}$ compactly evaluates depth-$d$ circuits with gates in $\Gamma$

nodes.name: Evaluate Complexity (Theorem 4.2.2)
nodes.statement: For circuit $C$ of depth $\le d$ and size $s$, the complexity of $\mathrm{Evaluate}_{E^{(d)}}$ is dominated by $\le s\ell d$ applications of $\mathrm{WeakEncrypt}_E$ and $\le s d$ applications of $\mathrm{Evaluate}_E$ to circuits in $D_E(\Gamma)$.

nodes.name: Semantic Security of Leveled Scheme (Theorem 4.2.3)
nodes.statement: Let $A$ $(t,\epsilon)$-break the semantic security of $E^{(d)}$. Then $\exists B$ that $(t',\epsilon')$-breaks $E$ with $t' \approx t\ell$ and $\epsilon' \ge \epsilon/(\ell(d+1))$.

nodes.name: FHE from KDM-Secure Bootstrappable Encryption (Theorem 4.3.2)
nodes.statement: Suppose $E$ is KDM-secure and bootstrappable wrt a universal gate set $\Gamma$. Then the scheme $E^*$ obtained by adding a self-loop of encrypted secret keys is semantically secure and fully homomorphic.

nodes.name: FHE from Bootstrappable Encryption via Random Oracle (Theorem 4.4.2)
nodes.statement: Suppose $E$ is leveled circuit-private and bootstrappable, $E^{(d)\dagger}$ and $E^*$ are the constructed schemes. If $E^{(d)\dagger}$ is semantically secure in the plain model and the depth to compute $H$ and invert $\star$ is $\le d$, then $E^*$ is semantically secure (in the random oracle model).

nodes.name: Correctness of Abstract Scheme (Theorem 5.2.6)
nodes.statement: Assume $C_E$ is a set of permitted circuits containing the identity circuit. Then $E$ is correct for $C_E$, i.e., $\mathrm{Decrypt}$ correctly decrypts valid ciphertexts.
assumptions: $C_E$ is a set of permitted circuits containing the identity

nodes.name: Security of Abstract Scheme via ICP (Theorem 5.3.1)
nodes.statement: If $A$ breaks the semantic security of $E$ with advantage $\epsilon$ (with $\mathrm{Samp}(B_I,x) = x + r\cdot s$ where $s$ generates principal ideal $I$), then $\exists B$ in about the same time solving ICP with advantage $\epsilon/2$.
assumptions: $A$ breaks semantic security of $E$ with advantage $\epsilon$
$\mathrm{Samp}(B_I,x) = x + r\cdot s$ with $s$ a generator of $I$

nodes.name: Circuit Depth vs. Error Expansion (Theorem 7.3.2)
nodes.statement: Suppose $r_E \ge 1$, $C$ has $\mathrm{Add}$ fan-in $\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)$, $\mathrm{Mult}$ fan-in $2$, depth $\le \log\log r_D - \log\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_E)$. Then $C(x_1,\ldots,x_t) \in B(r_D)$ for all $x_i \in B(r_E)$. In particular, $E$ correctly evaluates circuits of depth up to $\log\log r_{\mathrm{Dec}} - \log\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_{\mathrm{Enc}})$.
assumptions: $C$ has appropriate fan-in and depth bound
conclusions: $E$ correctly evaluates circuits up to depth $\log\log r_{\mathrm{Dec}} - \log\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_{\mathrm{Enc}})$

nodes.name: Polynomial Ring Expansion Factor (Theorem 7.4.1)
nodes.statement: Let $f(x)$ be monic of degree $n$. Let $F(x) = x^n\cdot f(1/x)$ and $g(x) = F(x)^{-1} \bmod x^{n-1}$. Then $\|u\times v\| \le \gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot\|u\|\cdot\|v\|$ where $\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R) \le \sqrt{2n}\cdot(1 + 2n\cdot\|f\|\cdot\|g\|)$.

nodes.name: Sparse-Polynomial Expansion Bound (Theorem 7.4.2)
nodes.statement: If $f(x) = x^n - h(x)$ with $\deg h \le n - (n-1)/k$ for some $k$, then $\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)$ is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ depending on $k$ and $\|h\|$.

nodes.name: Security via SplitKey Problem (Theorem 10.1.2)
nodes.statement: If $A$ breaks the semantic security of $E$ (the squashed scheme) with advantage $\epsilon$, then $\exists B_0, B_1$ in about the same time such that $B_0$'s advantage on the SplitKey Distinguishing Problem or $B_1$'s advantage against semantic security of $E^*$ is $\ge \epsilon/3$.
assumptions: $A$ breaks semantic security of $E$ with advantage $\epsilon$

nodes.name: Bootstrappability Condition for Squashed Scheme (Theorem 10.3.1)
nodes.statement: $E$ is bootstrappable when $\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)\cdot\log^{c_1}\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n) \le 2^{c_2}\cdot\tfrac{\log(r_{\mathrm{Dec}}/m)}{\log(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_{\mathrm{Enc}})}$, with $c_1, c_2$ constants and $m$ from Tweak redefinitions of $C_E$.

nodes.name: SplitKey Reduces to SVSSP (Theorem 11.1.3)
nodes.statement: Let $A$ decide concrete SplitKey Distinguishing with advantage $\epsilon$. Then $\exists B$ in about the same time solving SVSSP with advantage $(\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)/(2\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)))\cdot\epsilon$.

nodes.name: SVSSP Reduces to SSSP (Theorem 11.1.5)
nodes.statement: Assume $B_I$ and $\mathrm{IdealGen}$ make $\det(I), \det(J)$ distinct primes and $q/\det(IJ)$ super-polynomial. If $A$ decides SVSSP with advantage $\epsilon$, then $\exists B$ deciding SSSP with advantage $\epsilon/(2\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n))$ up to negligible factors.

nodes.name: Search-to-Decision SSSP (Theorem 11.1.7)
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ decides SSSP with non-negligible advantage in poly-time. Then $\exists B$ solving Search SSSP with probability $1/2$ in poly-time (using Goldreich-Levin).

nodes.name: Goldreich-Levin Theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: Given oracle access to a predictor $A$ for $\langle s, r\rangle$ from $r$ with non-negligible advantage, one can recover $s$ in polynomial time with high probability.

nodes.name: Class Field Theory Inertia Result (cited)
nodes.statement: Assume GRH. Let $K/E$ be a proper abelian extension. Then there exist primes of $E$ that are inert in $K$ in densities given by the Chebotarev density theorem.

nodes.name: Security via IIMP (Theorem 14.3.2)
nodes.statement: Let $s_{\mathrm{IIMP}} = s/\sqrt{2}$ where $s$ is the Gaussian deviation parameter in $E$, with $s_{\mathrm{IIMP}}/\sqrt{2}$ exceeding the smoothing parameter of $I$. If $A$ breaks semantic security of $E$ with advantage $\epsilon$, then $\exists B$ solving IIMP with advantage $\epsilon/2$ up to negligible factors.

nodes.name: IIMP Reduces to MIIMP (Theorem 14.4.2)
nodes.statement: Suppose $s_{\mathrm{MIIMP}} < s_{\mathrm{IIMP}}\epsilon/(n\cdot\max\{\|B_I\|\})$ and $[R:I]$ is prime. If $A$ solves IIMP with advantage $\epsilon$, then $\exists B$ solving MIIMP for an $\epsilon/2$ weighted fraction of bases $B^{pk}_J$ with overwhelming probability in time $O(1/\epsilon)$ times $A$'s.

nodes.name: MIIMP Reduces to HBDDP (Theorem 14.5.2)
nodes.statement: Suppose $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}} \le (s_{\mathrm{MIIMP}} - 2n\|B_I\|)/(\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot(\sqrt{n}/2))$. If $A$ solves MIIMP for an $\epsilon$ fraction of bases, then $\exists B$ solving HBDDP for an $\epsilon$ fraction of bases with overwhelming probability in polynomially larger time (provided $[R:I] = \mathrm{poly}(n)$).

nodes.name: HBDDP to IVIP via Regev's Quantum Reduction (Theorem 14.6.2)
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be an ideal lattice. Suppose $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}} \le s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}/(n^{1.5}\|f\|)$ and $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}} \le \lambda_1(J)/2$. If a classical algorithm $A$ solves $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$-HBDDP for $J$ (with probability $1$), then $\exists$ quantum algorithm $B$ solving $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$-IVIP for $J$.
nodes.origin_citation: Adapted from Regev's quantum BDD-to-SIVP reduction

nodes.name: RandomizeIdeal' Properties (Theorem 16.3.2)
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha \ge 1$, assuming RandomIdealGen is efficient, RandomizeIdeal' efficiently outputs a basis $B_J$ of an ideal $J$ along with the vector $v$, with $\det(J)$ in a controlled interval and $J$ statistically uniform.

nodes.name: WBDDP Reduces to HBDDP via RandomizeIdeal' (Theorem 16.3.3)
nodes.statement: Assume RandomIdealGen is efficient. If $A$ solves $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$-HBDDP for an $\epsilon$ fraction of average-case ideals (under RandomIdealGen's distribution), then there is an algorithm $B$ solving $s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}}$-WBDDP for any worst-case ideal $M$ with $\det(M) \in [N, 2N]$ when parameters relate appropriately.

nodes.name: RandomizeIdeal Produces Uniform Random Prime Ideal (Theorem 16.3.4)
nodes.statement: Let $I_{a,b}$ be invertible prime ideals of norm in $[a,b]$, with $|I_{a,b}|/b$ non-negligible, $\log b = \mathrm{poly}(n)$, $a^2 > 2N\cdot t_0^n$ (for $t_0 = t + s\sqrt{n}$, $s = \omega(\sqrt{\log n})$, $s = n^3\|f\|^3(b/N)^{1/n}\omega(\sqrt{\log n})$, $t \ge \gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot n^{1.5}\cdot s$). Given ideal $M$ of norm in $[N,2N]$ and a factoring oracle, RandomizeIdeal efficiently outputs a basis of an invertible prime ideal $J$ statistically uniform and independent of $M$, with $\mathrm{Nm}(J) \in [a,b]$.

nodes.name: Worst-Case to Average-Case Reduction for BDDP (Theorem 16.3.5)
nodes.statement: If $A$ solves $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$-HBDDP with overwhelming probability for an $\epsilon$ weighted fraction of invertible prime ideals $J \in I_{a,b}$ (with $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}} < \lambda_1(J)/2$), then $\exists B$ with running time $O(1/\epsilon)$ times $A$'s solving $s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}}$-WBDDP for any worst-case $M$ with $\det(M) \in [N,2N]$, when $2t\cdot s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}} + \sqrt{n} \le s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$.

nodes.name: Worst-Case to Average-Case for IVIP (Theorem 17.3.1)
nodes.statement: If $A$ solves $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$-IVIP for an $\epsilon$ weighted fraction of $J \in I_{a,b}$, then $\exists B$ in time $O(1/\epsilon)$ times $A$'s that solves IVIP for any worst-case $M$ with $\det(M) \in [N,2N]$ for parameter $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}/2t$.

nodes.name: WeakRandomIdealGen Uniform Sampling (Theorem 18.2.2)
nodes.statement: The WeakRandomIdealGen algorithm uniformly samples an invertible ideal $K \subset R$ with norm in $[a,b]$, running in time $b/(b-a)\cdot\mathrm{poly}(n, \log b)$.

nodes.name: IVIP Hardness by Lattice Determinant (Theorem 19.1.1)
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ solves $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$-IVIP whenever $\det(J) \in [d^n_{\mathrm{IVIP}}, 2d^n_{\mathrm{IVIP}}]$. Let $M$ have norm in $[N,2N]$ with $N \ge a$, and assume invertible prime ideals with norms in $[a,b]$ are not negligibly sparse. Then $\exists B$ solving IVIP for $M$ with parameter $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}/(2\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot n^{2.5}\cdot\|f\|\cdot g(n))$ for any $g(n) = \omega(\sqrt{\log n})$.

nodes.name: SIVP Reduces to ISIVP (Theorem 19.2.3)
nodes.statement: If $A$ solves $d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}}$-ISIVP, then $\exists B$ that solves $d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}}$-SIVP.

nodes.name: ISIVP Reduces to IVIP (Theorem 19.2.4)
nodes.statement: Let $d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}} = (3e)^{1/n}\cdot d_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$. Suppose $A$ solves IVIP for $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}} > 8\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot n^{2.5}\omega(\sqrt{\log n})$ for all ideals with $\det \ge d^n_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$. Then $\exists B$ solving $d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}}$-ISIVP in time $\approx \log d_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$ times $A$'s.

nodes.name: Summary of Security Reductions (Corollary 14.7.1)
nodes.statement: Under appropriate parameter settings, if $A$ breaks semantic security of $E$ with advantage $\epsilon$, then $\exists$ classical $B_1$ solving $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$-HBDDP for an $\epsilon/4$ fraction of bases in time $O([R:I]\cdot(1/\epsilon)\cdot\mathrm{time}(A))$, and a quantum algorithm solving $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$-IVIP for an $\epsilon/4$ fraction of bases.

nodes.name: Security on Worst-Case SIVP (Corollary 19.2.5)
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ solves $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$-IVIP for $s_{\mathrm{IVIP}} > 16\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)^2\cdot n^5\cdot\|f\|\cdot g(n)$ with $g = \omega(\log n)$, whenever $\det(J) \in [d^n_{\mathrm{IVIP}}, 2d^n_{\mathrm{IVIP}}]$ and prime ideals are not negligibly sparse. Then $\exists B$ solving worst-case $d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}}$-ISIVP with $d_{\mathrm{ISIVP}} = (3e)^{1/n}\cdot d_{\mathrm{IVIP}}$.

nodes.name: Abstract Scheme: KeyGen, Encrypt, Decrypt, Evaluate
nodes.statement: Abstract ring-and-ideal scheme: $\mathrm{KeyGen}$ runs $(B^{sk}_J, B^{pk}_J) \leftarrow \mathrm{IdealGen}(R,B_I)$; encryption samples $\psi' \leftarrow \mathrm{Samp}(B_I,\pi)$ and outputs $\psi \leftarrow \psi' \bmod B^{pk}_J$; decryption is $\pi = (\psi \bmod B^{sk}_J) \bmod B_I$.
output: Public key $pk = (R, B_I, B^{pk}_J, \mathrm{Samp})$, secret key $sk = pk \cup \{B^{sk}_J\}$

nodes.name: Recrypt (Bootstrapping Refresh)
nodes.statement: Refreshes a ciphertext $\psi_1$ encrypted under $pk_1$ to a fresh ciphertext under $pk_2$ by homomorphically evaluating $E$'s decryption circuit $D_E$ on encrypted secret key bits.
input: Encrypted secret-key bits $\langle\overline{sk_{1j}}\rangle$ (each bit of $sk_1$ encrypted under $pk_2$)

nodes.name: Generic Leveled FHE: KeyGen, Encrypt, Decrypt, Evaluate (E^(d))
nodes.statement: Constructs $E^{(d)}$ from a bootstrappable $E$: generates $d+1$ key pairs and a chain of encrypted secret keys, then evaluates by recursively augmenting each circuit level with $D_E$ and reducing.
input: Circuit $C$ of depth $\le d$ with gates in $\Gamma$
Tuple of input ciphertexts $\Psi$ encrypted under $pk_d$

nodes.name: Concrete Somewhat-Homomorphic Scheme over Ideal Lattices
nodes.statement: Instantiates the abstract scheme over $R = \mathbb{Z}[x]/(f(x))$: $\mathrm{Samp}(B_I,\pi)$ outputs $\pi + r\cdot s$ for short $r$; $\mathrm{IdealGen}$ outputs $B^{sk}_J$ inscribing a large sphere of radius $r_{\mathrm{Dec}}$; encryption reduces mod $B^{pk}_J$; decryption uses $\pi = \psi - B^{sk}_J\cdot\lfloor (B^{sk}_J)^{-1}\cdot\psi\rceil \bmod B_I$.

nodes.name: Squashing Transformation: SplitKey, ExpandCT, Decrypt
nodes.statement: Squashes $E^*$'s decryption: $\mathrm{SplitKey}$ produces a hint $\tau = \{t_1,\ldots,t_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)}\} \subset J^{-1}$ with secret sparse subset $S$ summing to $v^{sk^*}_J \bmod I$ and a 0/1 matrix $M$ encoding $S$. $\mathrm{ExpandCT}$ outputs $c_i = t_i\times\psi^* \bmod B_I$. $\mathrm{Decrypt}$ extracts the relevant $c_i$'s via $M$, sums them, rounds, subtracts.
output: Squashed scheme $E$ with new sk $M$ (sparse 0/1 matrix), pk extended with $\tau$
Expanded ciphertext $\psi$ that decrypts via shallow circuit

nodes.name: RandomizeIdeal (Worst-Case to Average-Case)
nodes.statement: Randomizes a worst-case ideal $M$ into a uniformly random invertible prime ideal $J$ of norm in $[a,b]$ statistically independent of $M$, by sampling a Gaussian $v$, factoring $L = M\cdot(v)$ with a factoring oracle, and rejection-sampling on the prime divisors.
input: Ring $R$, basis $B_M$ of ideal $M$ with norm in $[N,2N]$
Parameters $s, t, a, b$ satisfying smoothing and density conditions
output: Basis $B_J$ of an invertible prime ideal $J$ statistically uniform in $I_{a,b}$

nodes.name: RandomizeIdeal' (Classical Variant)
nodes.statement: Variant of RandomizeIdeal that does not require a factoring oracle on the worst-case ideal: uses an alternative ideal-randomization approach (alpha-scaling) to obtain efficient classical reductions, used in Section 18 to instantiate IdealGen.
output: Basis $B_K$ of invertible $K$, vector $v$, Hermite normal form $B_J$ of $J = K\cdot(v)/$...

nodes.name: WeakRandomIdealGen (Adapted Kalai's Algorithm)
nodes.statement: Generates a uniformly random invertible factored ideal $K \subset R$ with norm in $[a,b]$ by adapting Kalai's algorithm for random factored numbers to handle multiple ideals over the same prime.
output: Basis $B_K$ of invertible ideal $K$, factorization, with $\mathrm{Nm}(K) \in [a,b]$ uniform

nodes.name: Concrete IdealGen for Average-Case Distribution
nodes.statement: Instantiates $\mathrm{IdealGen}$ from WeakRandomizeIdeal: sets $B^{pk}_J = $ HNF $B_J$ from WeakRandomizeIdeal output, and $B^{sk}_J$ to be the rotation basis $B_v$ of $v$.
output: Public basis $B^{pk}_J$ (HNF), secret basis $B^{sk}_J$ (rotation basis of $v$)

nodes.name: Kalai's Algorithm for Random Factored Number
nodes.statement: Generates a uniformly random integer $1 \le N \le b$ with its prime factorization, by drawing a decreasing sequence of primes and rejection-sampling.

nodes.name: Recrypt Implies Proxy Re-Encryption
nodes.statement: The Recrypt algorithm yields a one-way proxy re-encryption scheme: the encrypted secret-key bits $\langle sk_{1j}\rangle$ act as a tag enabling an untrusted proxy to convert encryptions under $pk_1$ to encryptions under $pk_2$.

nodes.name: WeakEncrypt Relaxation
nodes.statement: Replacing $\mathrm{Encrypt}_E$ with a $\mathrm{WeakEncrypt}_E$ (whose image lies inside $\mathrm{Encrypt}_E$'s) in the Recrypt step preserves bootstrapping while reducing the cost of homomorphic decryption.

nodes.name: Boolean vs General Plaintext Spaces
nodes.statement: Bootstrapping requires representing decryption as a $\bmod\text{-}B_I$ circuit. Restricting plaintexts to $\{0,1\} \bmod B_I$ enables NAND emulation via $1 - x\times y$, but is wasteful when $\det(I)$ is large; this remains an open inefficiency.

nodes.name: Avoid Restricting Plaintext Space to {0,1} for Bootstrapping
nodes.statement: Find a way to bootstrap that uses all $\det(I)$ cosets of $I$ instead of restricting plaintexts to $\{0,1\} \bmod B_I$, despite the high-degree carry polynomials encountered in general 'base-$I$' addition.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2.6 (Correctness of Abstract Scheme)
nodes.statement: Decompose each $\psi_k = \pi_k + i_k + j_k$, expand $\mathrm{Evaluate}(pk,C,\Psi)$ in the ring, observe the result lies in $g(C)(\pi_1+i_1,\ldots) + J$, then take $\bmod B^{sk}_J$ then $\bmod B_I$ to recover $C(\vec\pi)$ when $C$ is permitted.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.3.2 (Circuit Depth vs. Error Expansion)
nodes.statement: By induction on circuit depth: at level $i$, values lie in $B((\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_{i-1})^2)$; iterating $d$ times yields $r_d \le (\gamma_{\mathrm{Mult}}(R)\cdot r_E)^{2^d}$, and the depth bound on $d$ ensures $r_d \le r_D$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10.1.2 (Squashing Security)
nodes.statement: Hybrid argument: define Game 0 (real semantic security) and Game 1 (challenger calls SplitKey on $\bot$ instead of $sk^*$). Construct $B_0$ distinguishing the games (advantage $\ge|\epsilon-\epsilon_0|/2$) and $B_1$ winning $E^*$'s semantic security from Game 1 (advantage $\epsilon_0$); one of them is $\ge\epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11.1.3 (SplitKey to SVSSP)
nodes.statement: Given SVSSP instance $(\tau, sk^*, pk^*)$, multiply by $B_{J^{-1}}$ and reduce mod $B_I$ to get $T'$; randomly add $v^{sk^*}_J$ (or $0$) into a uniformly random column $k$ to get $T$. Use $A$'s answer $\beta'$ and randomization $\beta$ to build $b' = \beta\oplus\beta'$, achieving advantage $(\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}/2\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}})\cdot\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 16.3.4 (RandomizeIdeal Output is Uniform)
nodes.statement: Show restart probability is non-overwhelming; show $J$ is selected iff $v \in JM^{-1}$; compute $\Pr[J] = \rho_{s,t\cdot e_1}(JM^{-1})/\rho_{s,t\cdot e_1}(M^{-1}) \approx 1/\det(J)$ via the smoothing-parameter Lemma 13.2.6, with Step 4 rejection sampling making this $1/b$ uniform.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 16.3.5 (WBDDP to HBDDP via RandomizeIdeal)
nodes.statement: Run RandomizeIdeal on $(M, u)$ to obtain $(B_J, v)$; set $t' = u\times v$ and $t = \lfloor t'\rceil \bmod B_J$; invoke $A$ on the HBDDP instance $(J,t)$ to get $y$; output $x = (y+c)/v$. Bound the error $\|z''\| \le 2t\cdot s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}} + \sqrt{n} \le s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$.

nodes.name: Define Game 0 and Game 1
nodes.statement: Game 0 is the real-world semantic security game for the squashed scheme $E$. Game 1 is identical except the challenger generates $\tau$ by calling $\mathrm{SplitKey}(\bot, pk^*)$ instead of $\mathrm{SplitKey}(sk^*, pk^*)$. Let $\epsilon$ and $\epsilon_0$ be $A$'s advantages in Game 0 and Game 1 respectively.

nodes.name: Construct $B_0$ to distinguish Games via SplitKey instance
nodes.statement: $B_0$ receives a SplitKey Distinguishing instance $(\tau, sk^*, pk^*)$ and runs $A$ on $pk = (pk^*, \tau)$. The simulation matches Game $b$ exactly, giving $B_0$'s advantage $\ge |\epsilon - \epsilon_0|/2$.

nodes.name: Construct $B_1$ attacking $E^*$ from Game 1 perspective
nodes.statement: $B_1$ obtains $pk^*$ from the $E^*$-challenger, runs $\mathrm{SplitKey}(\bot, pk^*)$ to get $\tau$, forwards $A$'s challenge to the $E^*$-challenger, and forwards back $\psi^*$ extended by $\mathrm{ExpandCT}$. The view matches Game 1, so $B_1$'s advantage equals $\epsilon_0$.

nodes.name: Combine bounds: at least one advantage exceeds $\epsilon/3$
nodes.statement: From $\mathrm{Adv}(B_0) \ge |\epsilon - \epsilon_0|/2$ and $\mathrm{Adv}(B_1) = \epsilon_0$, the maximum is $\ge \epsilon/3$ (worst case $\epsilon_0 = \epsilon/3$).

nodes.name: Bound restart probabilities in Steps 3 and 4
nodes.statement: By assumption $a/b$ is non-negligible (Step 3 succeeds with non-negligible probability) and by Lemma 15.2.3 there is non-negligible probability that $M\cdot(v)$ has an invertible prime ideal divisor with norm in $[a,b]$ (Step 4 succeeds), so the algorithm runs efficiently.

nodes.name: $J$ is chosen iff $v \in JM^{-1}$
nodes.statement: Use $\det(L) \le 2N\cdot t_0^n < a^2 \le \det(J)^2$ from the parameter conditions: an invertible prime $J$ of norm in $[a,b]$ dividing $L$ is unique. The 'only if' direction follows from $J + M^{-1}M = R$ since $J$ is invertible and $M^{-1}M$ has only singular factors.

nodes.name: Compute $\Pr[J] = \rho_{s,t\cdot e_1}(JM^{-1})/\rho_{s,t\cdot e_1}(M^{-1})$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 13.2.6 (smoothing-parameter ratio) this equals $\det(M^{-1})/\det(JM^{-1}) = 1/\det(J)$ up to a factor negligibly close to $1$, provided $s$ exceeds the smoothing parameter of $JM^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Verify $s$ exceeds the smoothing parameter of $JM^{-1}$
nodes.statement: Bound $s = n^3\|f\|^3(b/N)^{1/n}\omega(\sqrt{\log n}) \ge n\|f\|\det(JM^{-1})^{1/n}\omega(\sqrt{\log n}) \ge \lambda_n(JM^{-1})\omega(\sqrt{\log n})$ via the transference lemmas of Chapter 8.2.

nodes.name: Step 4 rejection sampling adjusts to uniform $1/b$
nodes.statement: Step 4 outputs with probability $\det(J)/b$, multiplying $\Pr[J] \approx 1/\det(J)$ to give $1/b$ — uniform over invertible prime ideals with norm in $[a,b]$ and independent of $M$.

nodes.name: Run RandomizeIdeal on the WBDDP instance
nodes.statement: Run $(B_J, v) \leftarrow \mathrm{RandomizeIdeal}(R, B_M, N, s, t, a, b)$ to obtain a uniformly random invertible prime $J$ of norm in $[a,b]$, statistically independent of $M$.

nodes.name: Form HBDDP target
nodes.statement: Set $t' \leftarrow u\times v$ and $t \leftarrow \lfloor t'\rceil \bmod B_J$; let $c \in [-1/2, 1/2)^n$ be such that $t' - t - c \in J$.

nodes.name: Verify $(J,t)$ is a valid HBDDP instance
nodes.statement: Decompose $u = m + z$ with $\|z\| \le s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}}$. Then $t' = m' + z'$ with $m' \in M\cdot(v) \subseteq J$ and $\|z'\| \le 2t\cdot s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}}$ (using $v \in t\cdot e_1 + B(s\sqrt{n})$). Rounding to $t$ shifts by $\le \sqrt{n}$ giving $t = j + z''$ with $\|z''\| \le 2t\cdot s_{\mathrm{WBDDP}} + \sqrt{n} \le s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$.

nodes.name: Invoke $A$ on the HBDDP instance
nodes.statement: $A$ returns $y$ with $\|y\| < s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}}$ and $t - y \in J$. Since $z''$ is also a valid solution and $s_{\mathrm{HBDDP}} < \lambda_1(J)/2$, uniqueness gives $y = z''$.

nodes.name: Recover WBDDP solution
nodes.statement: Compute $x \leftarrow (y + c)/v$. Then $z'' + c = z'$ so $z'/v = z$, recovering the original WBDDP error vector.

nodes.name: SplitKey: generate sparse-subset hint
nodes.statement: Sample $t_1, \ldots, t_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)-1}$ uniformly in $J^{-1} \cap P(B_I)$; set $t_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)} \leftarrow v^{sk^*}_J - \sum_{i=1}^{\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)-1} t_i \bmod B_I$, then permute. Set the secret key $sk = M$, a $\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n) \times \gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)$ 0/1 matrix encoding the subset $S$.

nodes.name: ExpandCT: precompute $c_i = t_i \times \psi^* \bmod B_I$
nodes.statement: For each $i \in [1, \gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)]$, output $c_i \leftarrow t_i \times \psi^* \bmod B_I$, expanding the ciphertext from $\psi^*$ to $(\psi^*, c_1, \ldots, c_{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)})$.

nodes.name: Decrypt Step 0: select via $M$
nodes.statement: Set $w_{ij} \leftarrow M_{ij}\cdot c_j$ for all $i, j$ (constant-depth multiplication).

nodes.name: Decrypt Step 1: extract sparse subset sums
nodes.statement: Set $x_i \leftarrow \sum_{j=1}^{\gamma_{\mathrm{setsize}}(n)} w_{ij}$. Each row of $M$ has a unique $1$, so the sum is constant-depth (XOR-style; no carries).

nodes.name: Decrypt Step 2: round via symmetric polynomials (Lemma 9.0.3)
nodes.statement: From $x_1, \ldots, x_{\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)}$, generate $y_1, \ldots, y_{\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n)+1}$ with $\sum y_i = \lfloor\sum x_i\rceil$ using a circuit of depth $\le c\cdot(\log\gamma_{\mathrm{subsetsize}}(n))^{1+o(1)}$.

nodes.name: Decrypt Step 3: subtract and reduce
nodes.statement: Compute $\pi \leftarrow \psi^* - (\sum y_i) \bmod B_I$ (constant depth via polynomial-fan-in $\mathrm{Add}_{B_I}$).

nodes.name: Sample Gaussian vector $v$ near $t\cdot e_1$
nodes.statement: Sample $v \leftarrow D_{M^{-1}, s, t\cdot e_1}$ (e.g. via the GPV algorithm with the standard basis $\{e_i\}$ of $M^{-1}$); set $L \leftarrow M\cdot(v)$.

nodes.name: Factor $L$ via factoring oracle
nodes.statement: Use the factoring oracle to compute bases of the invertible prime ideal divisors $\{p_i\}$ of $L$.

nodes.name: Select prime divisor of norm in $[a,b]$, else restart
nodes.statement: If some $p_i \in \{p_j\}$ has norm in $[a,b]$, set $J \leftarrow p_i$; otherwise restart from Step 1.

nodes.name: Rejection sample $J$ with probability $\det(J)/b$
nodes.statement: With probability $\det(J)/b$ output $(B_J, v)$; otherwise restart. This rejection step yields $\Pr[J] = 1/b$ uniform.

nodes.name: KeyGen: generate $d+1$ key chain
nodes.statement: For $i \in [0, d]$ run $(sk_i, pk_i) \leftarrow \mathrm{KeyGen}_E(\lambda)$. For $i \in [1,d], j \in [1,\ell]$ encrypt the $j$th bit of $sk_i$ under $pk_{i-1}$ to get $\overline{sk_{ij}}$. Output $sk^{(d)} = sk_0$, $pk^{(d)} = (\langle pk_i\rangle, \langle\overline{sk_{ij}}\rangle)$.

nodes.name: Evaluate: recursive Augment + Reduce
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Evaluate}_{E^{(\delta)}}(pk^{(\delta)}, C_\delta, \Psi_\delta)$: if $\delta = 0$ return $\Psi_0$; else Augment $C_\delta$ with $D_E$ (replacing each input ciphertext by encrypted-sk + encrypted-bit pairs), Reduce to a depth-$\delta-1$ circuit by evaluating the top level, recurse on $\mathrm{Evaluate}_{E^{(\delta-1)}}$.

nodes.name: Decrypt: apply $D_E$ at base level
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Decrypt}_{E^{(d)}}(sk^{(d)}, \psi)$ outputs $\mathrm{Decrypt}_E(sk_0, \psi)$ (the ciphertext should be encrypted under $pk_0$).
